paper.central_claim: Skills-Coach is an automated framework (task generation, Training-Free-GRPO optimization of skill instructions and code, comparative execution, traceable evaluation with retain/discard decisions) that self-evolves LLM-agent skills without human intervention, raising skill capability on the 48-skill Skill-X benchmark (avg score 0.378 -> 0.84, pass rate 33.59% -> 88.02%).
paper.title: Skills-Coach: A Self-Evolving Skill Optimizer via Training-Free GRPO

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; null by contract.

evidence.quote: Skills-Coach achieves significant performance improvements in skill capability across a wide range of categories
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim; author-reported.

evidence.quote: This paradigm has engendered a skill ecosystem characterized by abundant volume but fragmented coverage
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: fragmented coverage of skills (asserted with generic citations and the 56,000-skill Clawhub count); the method polishes existing skills rather than adding coverage.

evidence.quote: Can an agent autonomously explore the capability boundaries of its existing skills and proactively expand them to achieve skill self-evolution?
evidence.support_explanation: Research question; 'expand' is evaluated only as higher scores on generated tasks for the same skill.

evidence.quote: Instead, it estimates task completion by verifying the presence of evaluation-criteria-related keywords (such as "error handling" and "save") within the skill instruction, combined with deterministic random numbers generated from a hash of the skill’s content.
evidence.support_explanation: Virtual mode scores skills by keyword presence plus hash-seeded random numbers, i.e. it does not measure execution.

evidence.quote: Execution defaults to real mode for both optimization-time execution and final evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Reported experiments are stated to run in real mode; for instruction-only skills real-mode scoring is LLM judgement of the text (E011).

evidence.quote: In task generation, the current pipeline creates 12 training tasks and 8 test tasks, with an even split between difficulty levels (6 standard + 6 advanced for training, 4 standard + 4 advanced for testing).
evidence.support_explanation: Per-skill test set is only 8 pipeline-generated tasks.

evidence.quote: During Training-Free GRPO optimization, each epoch generates 3 rollout variants (group_size=3) for the current skill version and evaluates them on the training set, rather than generating variants per individual task.
evidence.support_explanation: Optimization is a best-of-3 variant selection per epoch over 3 epochs; the group-relative experience extraction of Training-Free GRPO is not described.

evidence.quote: For LLM-powered optimization/fixing components, the default model is claude-sonnet-4-6 (with heuristic fallbacks when API-based generation is unavailable).
evidence.support_explanation: Same LLM family drives optimization/fixing; generation and judging model for tasks/evaluation not separated in the text.

evidence.quote: Notably, tasks within the test set maintain a difficulty level commensurate with the training set but feature entirely distinct contexts, rigorously assessing generalization capabilities over memorization.
evidence.support_explanation: Claimed train/test isolation; both sets are produced by the same generator from the same skill specification.

evidence.quote: As all optimization decisions and performance metrics are derived from these tasks, their generation quality directly determines the accuracy and efficacy of the entire optimization pipeline.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors acknowledge that the self-generated tasks define both the optimization signal and the metric.

evidence.quote: For instruction-only skills, LLMs are employed to conduct in-depth evaluations across eight dimensions: structural integrity, practicality, example quality, technical depth, clarity, command coverage, error handling, and advanced scenario adaptability.
evidence.support_explanation: 29 of 48 skills are scored by an LLM on documentation-quality dimensions rather than by an agent completing tasks.

evidence.quote: Clear concise language with average sentence length < 30 words
evidence.support_explanation: Rubric items are surface/documentation checks (sentence length, number of examples, sections present), which an optimizer can satisfy by restructuring text.

evidence.quote: Multiple concrete examples with at least 3 different real-world scenarios
evidence.support_explanation: Another form-based criterion; shows the metric rewards presence of document features.
All-skills baseline row: avg score 0.378, pass rate 33.59%.
All-skills optimized row; no uncertainty; (+0.47) is inconsistent with 0.84-0.378 = 0.462 (minor).

evidence.quote: (4) Decision Rigor: retention decisions are grounded in explicit mathematical rules, eliminating subjective judgment
evidence.support_explanation: Retain/discard rule is asserted but its thresholds and statistic are not given; evaluation data are the test-set results.

evidence.quote: that runs both the original and optimized versions of the target skill against all test tasks, systematically capturing outputs and execution logs for subsequent evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: The same test-task results feed the evaluation and, per Sec 1, the retention decision.

evidence.quote: It systematically calculates comprehensive metrics, performs comparative analysis, and informs data-driven retention decisions.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention is decided on the comparison between original and optimized versions on the test results.

evidence.quote: Notably, the module accelerates training time from hours to minutes, reduces data requirements from thousands of samples to merely dozens, while simultaneously mitigating overfitting risks and demonstrating superior generalization and cross-domain transfer capabilities.
evidence.support_explanation: Efficiency, overfitting and transfer claims are not supported by any comparison or cost measurement in the paper.
A widely used skill scoring 0.0 originally and 1.0 after optimization suggests rubric/task mismatch rather than a broken skill; typical of the 23 'Exceptional' cases.
No skill in the 48-row table has a negative or zero change except five already at 1.0; no regressions or discarded rewrites are reported.

evidence.quote: Concurrently, it must ensure that newly generated skills remain consistent and complementary with the existing skill ecosystem, thereby preventing capability degradation or conflicts.
evidence.support_explanation: Stated requirement; no mechanism or evaluation of ecosystem consistency or conflict appears in the method or experiments.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, a task is deemed "passed" if its score meets or exceeds a predefined threshold (defaulting to 70% of the maximum possible score).
evidence.support_explanation: Pass rate depends on a 70% threshold over rubric points.

evidence.quote: For code-inclusive skills, the assessment focuses on deterministic outcomes, including error-free command execution, successful output generation, format validity, expected data matching, and the robustness of handling complex scenarios.
evidence.support_explanation: For 19 code-inclusive skills checks are execution-based, a stronger measurement than the LLM-judged text rubric, but still on generated tasks with generated criteria.

evidence.quote: To ensure objectivity, all generated tasks are paired with automated validation criteria, utilizing metrics like output file existence, specific keyword inclusion, and regular expression compliance.
evidence.support_explanation: Validation criteria are automatically generated and shallow (existence, keywords, regex).

evidence.quote: First, we formalize the skill self-evolution problem and propose an automated solution that requires no human intervention, significantly reducing the burden on skill developers and maintainers.
evidence.support_explanation: No formalization or developer-effort measurement appears in the read text.

signatures.operation: Training-Free GRPO instruction optimization (3 variants per epoch, 3 epochs, select best on training set) plus code optimization (rule-driven optimizer, LLM command optimizer, auto-fixer, <=2 fix-test rounds)
signatures.conditions: Run per target skill in real mode
signatures.feedback: Pass/score on generated training tasks; failure analyses; LLM judgement of the document for instruction-only skills

signatures.persistence: Optimized skill files plus report; storage/versioning/rollback not described
signatures.later_use: Not shown: no downstream agent uses the retained skill; later use is the 8 generated test tasks
signatures.failure_boundary: Metric-aligned rewriting may not improve real utility; virtual mode is non-executing; ecosystem conflicts untreated

signatures.information: Skill specification parsed by regular expressions and structured parsing
signatures.operation: LLM generates standard/advanced/boundary tasks and automated validation criteria; evaluator scores outputs

gap.author_gap: The skill ecosystem has abundant volume but fragmented coverage; individually authored skills handle localized cases and leave functional gaps.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible practitioner problem but asserted with generic citations; the method does not expand coverage, it raises scores of existing skills on tasks generated from their own specification. The residue 'skills perform poorly on boundary tasks' is evidenced only by the authors' own low baseline scores.
gap.lineage: Prompt optimization (OPRO/TextGrad/DSPy-style, cited as method sources) and Training-Free GRPO -> reflection/self-refine -> skill ecosystems (Anthropic Agent Skills, Clawhub).
gap.closest_adjacent: Skill-evolution systems such as skill-creator and self-evolving-skill appear only as benchmark items being optimized; no skill-optimization baseline is compared.
gap.residue: Automated improvement of third-party skills without human intervention.
gap.stakes: Not quantified; 56,000 skills exist on Clawhub.
gap.remaining_gap: Real downstream agent success with optimized skills, versus alternative optimizers, ecosystem consistency, cost.
gap.unresolved: Whether score gains reflect utility or rubric conformity.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Signature steps executed: missing supervision identified, tasks/criteria/scores derived from the model and the artifact specification, artifact adapted on that signal. Sub-card tactics C08 (generate synthetic instances then a quality gate then retrain) and C26 (comparative/scalar rewards from a non-human judge optimized contrastively) are partially analogous but the adapted object is a text/code artifact, not a trained model, so no sub-card is assigned.

matches.reason: Parent fits the operation; fit is partial because the manufactured signal is also the evaluation metric.

claims.text: Skills-Coach significantly improves skill capability on Skill-X.
claims.setting: 48 public skills (29 instruction-only, 19 code-inclusive); claude-sonnet-4-6; 3 epochs; real mode
claims.selection_vs_test: 12 generated training tasks vs 8 generated test tasks per skill, same generator and rubric; retention decision on test results
claims.result_denominator: Avg 0.378 -> 0.84; pass 33.59% -> 88.02%; per-skill Table 2 (no regressions listed); single run, 8 tasks per skill
claims.counterevidence: Metric is a generated rubric; instruction-only skills judged on document features; baselines scoring 0.0 for popular skills; no alternative optimizer
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported: pipeline-rewritten skills score higher than originals on the pipeline's own generated tasks and rubric.

claims.text: Training-Free GRPO is an efficient alternative to parameter optimization (minutes vs hours, dozens vs thousands of samples).
Skills self-evolve in a closed loop without human intervention and stay consistent with the skill ecosystem.
claims.result_denominator: Single optimization pass per skill; no multi-round or downstream reuse
claims.allowed_conclusion: One-shot automated optimization; closed-loop retained use and ecosystem consistency not shown.

claims.text: Gains are larger for code-inclusive skills and advanced tasks.
claims.result_denominator: Code +55.92 pp pass, advanced +48.90 vs standard +44.43 in pass-rate points
claims.counterevidence: Different scoring modes (execution vs LLM-judged) across the two groups
claims.allowed_conclusion: Descriptive pattern within the author's metric.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: on 48 public skills the pipeline's rewritten skill files score higher than the originals on 8 pipeline-generated test tasks per skill under the pipeline's own rubric (execution-based checks for 19 code skills, LLM-judged documentation dimensions for 29 instruction skills). Not shown: improved real agent task success, retained reuse, advantage over simple rewrites or other optimizers, or any cost. Held at task because evaluation tasks, rubric and retention decision come from the same pipeline.
assessment.unresolved: Metric validity (Goodhart), alternative optimizer baselines, downstream use, ecosystem consistency, cost, variance.

G.reason: Fragmented-coverage framing is plausible but asserted with generic citations, and the method does not address coverage; the nearest neighbours (skill-creator, self-evolving-skill, prompt optimizers such as TextGrad/DSPy used as method sources) are not positioned as comparators. Between the 0 and 2 anchors.

M.reason: Concrete pipeline (generated tasks, grouped variant selection, rule/LLM/auto-fix code optimization, paired comparison, retain/discard) and sensible use of execution evidence for code skills; but the Training-Free GRPO step reduces to best-of-3 selection as described, there is no argument that rubric-driven edits improve real use, and the optimization signal is the evaluation metric.

X.reason: Hyperparameters, isolation and execution modes are well specified; retention rule, persistence/versioning, rollback, conflict handling with existing skills (stated as a requirement, E022), and later reading by an agent are missing or not shown.

E.measurement.reason: Code-skill checks are execution-based, but tasks and criteria are generated by the optimizing pipeline and are shallow (existence, keywords, regex); 29 of 48 skills are scored by an LLM on documentation-form criteria that an optimizer can satisfy by restructuring; no independent or downstream measure and no trivial rubric-stuffing baseline.

E.causality.reason: Only original-vs-optimized is reported; no ablation of GRPO selection vs one-shot rewrite, of auto-fix, of task generation, and no alternative optimizer or equal-budget baseline, so the gain cannot be attributed to the claimed mechanism rather than rubric-conforming rewriting.

E.holdout.reason: Separate 12/8 train/test split per skill is a start, but both sets come from the same generator and spec, retention decisions use the test comparison, no external tasks or downstream agent runs, and widely known public skills may be familiar to the model.

E.statistics.reason: Per-skill results are tabulated (implied denominators of 8 tasks) and no regressions are shown, but a single run, no intervals or variance, and aggregated means over very small per-skill test sets.

E.cost.reason: Optimization budget parameters (epochs, group size, task counts, fix rounds, model) are stated, but no tokens, calls, wall-clock or dollars, and the hours-to-minutes and thousands-to-dozens efficiency claims are untested.

rationale: 对 48 个现成 Skill 的自动重写与对比保留，分数大幅上升；但任务、规则、评审同源，指令类 Skill 以文档形式打分，无替代优化器与下游验证，成本未测，停在 task 级。
